chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr from Abd al-A'la from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'A man threw the Jamarah with six pebbles, and one fell among the pebbles.' He said: 'He should return it, if he wishes, immediately, or if he wishes, the next day when he intends to throw, and he should not take from the pebbles of the Jamarat.'
And I asked him about a man who threw the Jamarah of al-Aqabah with six pebbles, and one fell into the carrying case. He said: 'He should return it.'
And whoever knows that one pebble is missing but does not know from which of the Jamarat it is missing, let him throw one pebble at each of the Jamarat.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim loses a pebble or is unsure which Jamarah it was thrown at during Hajj?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of minor errors during the Ramy al-Jamarat, emphasizing flexibility by allowing the missed pebble to be replaced either immediately or the following day without requiring a new pebble from the main pile. It further establishes the principle of precaution (ihtiyat) by mandating that if the specific missed Jamarah is unknown, the pilgrim must throw an additional pebble at each of the three Jamarat to ensure the ritual's validity. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ensuring the completeness of Hajj pillars while accommodating practical difficulties faced by pilgrims.
